newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Nomura maintains 'sell' on Hungary's Egis.
newsitem.headline: Nomura maintains 'sell' on Hungary's Egis.

text.p: Nomura Equity Research said on Tuesday it maintained its 'sell' recommendation on shares in Hungarian pharmaceuticals company Egis Gyogyszergyar Rt after its first half earnings report.
"After a weak Q1, Egis has produced H1 figures that are even worse," analysts Frances Cloud and Matthew Arnold said in a company update.
"To make matters worse, increased working capital levels are eating into the company's cash pile, with the result that financial income for the year is likely to be well down on 1996," they said.
Egis's first-half after-tax profit fell to 3.033 billion forints from 3.314 billion forints in the same period of 1996.
Its exports rose 13 percent in dollar terms, but its domestic sales declined.
The analysts said there was little relief in sight in the short-term, particularly since Hungary's pricing system is set to get even tougher.
"We believe that there is downside in the share price to 9,000 forints and maintain our sell recommendation," they said.
